title: Pause and park
summary: Mode parked or turn posture waiting declares intentional pause. A paused work-claim holder remains parked as activity ages; silence alone never declares pause. Prompts, message-only turns, events query and items progress-log bookkeeping preserve parked mode and its reason. Ordinary reads and other successful work end the park. Arm a Claude Monitor before parking as the final action of the turn. Successful work or an explicit mode wait ends it; delayed activity cannot clear a newer park. Capacity recovery skips parked sessions. A holder schedules the earliest useful timed recheck with sessions.wake.schedule when evidence depends on time or traffic. Before parking on another item, record the merge or delivery wait through items.dependency.add; a dependency_cycle refusal must be resolved before parking. The held item’s own release wait needs no self-edge. A merge whose item owes nothing after deploy releases its work claim and does not park; the release closes the item without a holder. The Sessions page Active filter excludes sessions with native_process_gone_at set. Parked sessions remain visible under Parked with their held claims; process-gone parked workers use no machine lane until resumed. Claude Monitor resumes the current turn; ending that turn closes its reader. The harness capability evidence names this limit without changing idle_wake.
